newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CLEMENS IMPROVES TO 10-0 WITH WIN OVER ATHLETICS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLEMENS IMPROVES TO 10-0 WITH WIN OVER ATHLETICS.

text.p: Roger Clemens became the first 10-game winner in the majors and Joe Carter homered to cap an eight-run fourth inning Saturday as the Toronto Blue Jays demolished the Oakland Athletics 13-3.

Clemens (10-0) pitched eight innings and allowed two runs and eight hits. The big righthander struck out only four but benefitted from four double plays. The A's output actually raised Clemens's earned run average from 1.81 to 1.85.

"Roger has done a tremendous job for this club," said Toronto (26-25) manager Cito Gaston. "Without him, we're probably in last-place. I would say he's probably pitching as well as he's ever pitched."
Clemens entered the game with a 10-11 lifetime mark against Oakland, the only team he did not have a winning record against.
"I was really fortunate that our hitters put the big numbers up," said Clemens. "That makes a big difference, especially when they do it early."

Catcher Charlie O'Brien, shortstop Alex Gonzalez and second baseman Tilson Brito -- the bottom three hitters in Toronto's order -- went 10-for-13 with five RBI and five runs scored. The Jays had a season-high 19 hits in the game.
The eight-run fourth made it smooth sailing for Clemens.

"He's (Clemens) got great stuff, no doubt about it," said Oakland's Jason Giambi, who had two hits and an RBI. "That's why he's 10-0 now. He's been that way his whole career. You know you're going against the best."
The win snapped the Blue Jays' four-game losing streak.

In Baltimore, Tony Tarasco, Cal Ripken and Jeffrey Hammonds all homered and drove in two runs as the Baltimore Orioles overcame a four-run deficit to win their fifth straight game, 8-5, over the Cleveland Indians.
The Indians jumped out to a 4-0 lead in the first against Orioles starter Mike Johnson, but Baltimore rallied and tied it at 5-5 on Roberto Alomar's RBI single in the sixth.
The Orioles took the lead an inning later as Ripken led off with his ninth homer and Hammonds belted his fifth.
Shawn Boskie (3-2) pitched 3 2/3 scoreless innings of relief for the win.
In Boston, Andy Pettitte allowed two runs and struck out eight over 7 1/3 innings and Paul O'Neill hit two solo homers to lead the New York Yankees to a 7-2 win over the Red Sox.

Pettitte (7-3) snapped a personal two-game losing skid and earned his first career decision in Fenway Park. "If you make good pitches and you keep the hitters off balance, they're not going to drive the ball off you," he said. "I was able to do that today."
O'Neill, batting third for the first time this season, homered in the fifth and seventh innings off Boston knuckleballer Tim Wakefield and also had an RBI single.
At Texas, Rusty Greer homered and drove in a pair of runs and Julio Santana outdueled Kevin Appier as the Texas Rangers beat the Kansas City Royals 3-1.
Greer drove in a run with a fielder's choice groundout in the first and followed Ivan Rodriguez's homer with his sixth homer in the third for the Rangers.
Santana (3-2), who had allowed 14 runs in his last two starts, went 6 2/3 innings, allowing one run and seven hits. John Wetteland got the final three outs for his 12th save.
Appier (4-4) allowed three runs and eight hits in seven innings with three walks and nine strikeouts. He failed in his fifth attempt for his 100th career win.
"It seems like I've been pitching pretty well on average, but things haven't been working out for us lately overall," Appier said.

In Milwaukee, Jeromy Burnitz hit a pair of homers and Antone Williamson's pinch-hit double in the bottom of the seventh inning snapped a tie, leading the Milwaukee Brewers past the Chicago White Sox 4-3 for their third straight win.

The game was tied in the seventh when Dave Nilsson led off with a double off Jaime Navarro (4-4). Williamson hit for Matt Mieske and lined a 0-2 pitch into right field for his first career hit, giving the Brewers a 3-2 lead.
Ben McDonald (6-3) improved to 4-0 at home this season.
In Seattle, the Tigers scored three runs in the first inning to back to the pitching of Omar Olivares as Detroit posted their fifth win in six games with a 4-2 decision over the Seattle Mariners.

Olivares (4-3) allowed two runs and seven hits and struck out six without walking a batter in improving to 4-0 lifetime against the Mariners. Todd Jones struck out two in a perfect ninth inning for his fifth save.
In Anaheim, Dave Hollins homered twice and knocked in four runs as the Anaheim Angels beat the Minnesota Twins 5-3.
Hollins, who went 3-for-4, hit a solo homer in the first and a three-run shot in the third off Scott Aldred (2-8).
Chuck Finley (3-4) earned the win.
